plan.title: KO x drug interaction in brain bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question — does the drug act differently in knockout than in wild type — is a genotype x treatment interaction, and the design supports it directly: a balanced 2x2 factorial (genotype WT/KO x treatment vehicle/drug), 4 biological replicates per cell, 16 samples, 12,000 genes of raw salmon-derived integer counts in counts.csv with the sample table in metadata.csv. The counts matrix is listed as 12000 x 17 (gene symbol column plus 16 sample columns), matching the 16 rows of metadata.

The plan follows the DESeq2 interaction route. T1S1 does sample-structure QC on the raw counts (blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) coloured by genotype and treatment, to see whether the four cells separate at all and whether any of the 16 samples is misplaced relative to its declared cell — this is also the only opportunity to catch a swapped genotype/treatment label before the model. T1S2 fits ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with WT and vehicle set as explicit reference levels, and produces three result tables per gene: the drug effect in WT (the treatment main effect at the reference genotype), the drug effect in KO (main effect plus interaction), and the interaction contrast itself, which is the literal answer to the question. Log fold changes are shrunk with ashr because the KO simple effect is a sum of coefficients rather than a single coefficient; p-values come from the unshrunken fit. BH within each contrast at alpha 0.05, independent filtering on, p-value histograms inspected first. T1S2b runs the same design through edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test as an independent second method; the intersection is the high-confidence set.

The honest caveat, stated up front and carried into every output: an interaction coefficient is a difference of differences, so its standard error is roughly double that of a simple effect, and at n=4 per cell the power to detect it is low. A short or empty interaction list is a plausible and interpretable outcome — it means the data do not resolve a genotype-dependent drug effect at this sample size, not that the drug acts identically. Because of that, T2S1 runs preranked fgsea (ranking on the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed choice is settled in favour of the Wald stat, which scales effect by its uncertainty) on the full ranked list of every tested gene for each of the three contrasts separately, including the interaction. A coordinated pathway-level shift can be visible where no single gene passes FDR. Hallmark is the first pass; GO BP is the staged second collection (Reactome is not in this reference store, which the report must state in place of it). T1S3 assembles the report: the two simple effects and the interaction side by side, the reference levels named, MA and dispersion plots, count-outlier NAs separated from independent-filtering NAs, the two-method overlap, leading-edge genes per significant set, and a full reproducibility record.

GSEA on the full ranked list is the right instrument for that; an over-representation test on a short significant list would have no power. The reference store holds MSigDB human hallmark and human GO (BP/CC/MF) but no Reactome collection, so GO BP substitutes as the second collection and the report must say so.
acceptance_criteria: Three separate enrichment result tables, one per contrast, never pooled across contrasts
Ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat), stated explicitly in the output alongside the reasoning for the choice
Full ranked list of tested genes used as input — no significance or fold-change thresholding before the test
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes, and the window reported
Gene set collection names and versions reported; if the second collection is GO BP because Reactome is absent from the reference store, that substitution is stated in the output
Leading-edge genes with their gene-level statistic listed per significant set, and leading-edge overlap between reported sets marked
Redundant significant sets collapsed to representatives, with the uncollapsed table retained as a supplement
A random seed is set for the permutation step and recorded
constraints: Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic; the disputed ranking-metric choice is settled here in favour of the Wald stat because it scales the effect by its uncertainty — do not rank by unshrunken log2 fold change alone or by a signed p-value with ties
Use the full ranked list of all tested genes, not a thresholded list
Run enrichment once per contrast; do not pool genes across the three contrasts
Set the gene set size window to min 15, max 500, applied after intersection with the tested genes
Human gene sets only, matched to the Homo sapiens dataset
Set and record a random seed for the permutation-based p-values

If fewer than about 50 genes pass FDR in a contrast, do not run an over-representation test on that list — the ranked test on the full list is the method, and the size of the significant list is stated
caveats: Enrichment results depend strongly on the method and the collection; present significant sets as hypotheses for follow-up, not as established findings
GO BP is a nested hierarchy, so parent and child sets share members and significant hits arrive in correlated blocks — collapse before counting them as findings
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment on count data; the ranked test on the tested-gene universe mitigates but does not remove this — state it

An enriched set in the interaction contrast means the ranking of that set's genes is shifted by the difference of drug effects between genotypes; it does not identify the direction in either genotype on its own, so read it against the two simple-effect results

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list per contrast (R-0107@976c, R-0104@34a4); disputed rank metric R-0108@409f settled on the Wald statistic per R-0099@0a77; Hallmark first (R-0048@500d), with GO BP as the staged second collection since Reactome is not in this reference store.

steps.name: Interaction report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the evidence, stated with its uncertainty, that the drug acts differently in KO than in WT brain?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Present per gene, side by side: the drug effect in WT, the drug effect in KO, and the interaction contrast, with the reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle) named beside the tables and each contrast labelled. Include the MA plot and the dispersion plot from the DESeq2 fit before the gene tables. Give unshrunken log2FoldChange, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE for every reported gene, ranking and plotting on the shrunken value. State the design formula, package versions, thresholds (BH, alpha 0.05, FDR per contrast), the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, and the number of DE genes per contrast. Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set. For enrichment, state the collection and version, the Wald-statistic ranking metric, the tested-gene universe, the size window, and the leading-edge genes per significant set. Attach sessionInfo, the random seeds used, and the gene-set collection version. Close with an explicit power statement for the interaction test at n=4 per cell.
steps.context: The interaction is the research question, and it is the least well-powered quantity in the design. The report's job is to make the strength of the evidence legible rather than to produce a headline.
acceptance_criteria: Simple effect in WT, simple effect in KO, and the interaction contrast appear side by side per gene, with reference levels named
MA plot and dispersion plot appear before the gene tables, each with a sentence on what it shows
Gene tables carry unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold change plus lfcSE; ranking and plots use the shrunken value; p-values are from the unshrunken fit
Method, package versions, design formula, contrasts, thresholds, n tested and n DE per contrast are all stated
DESeq2/edgeR intersection reported as the high-confidence set, method-specific calls listed separately
Enrichment reporting includes collection and version, ranking metric, universe, size window, and per-set leading-edge genes
Reproducibility record attached: sessionInfo, package versions, random seeds, gene set collection version

An explicit statement of the power limitation of the interaction test at 4 replicates per cell, and of the fact that a non-significant interaction does not establish that the drug acts identically in both genotypes
No causal or mechanistic claim is made that the contrasts do not support
constraints: Report the two simple effects and the interaction contrast together; never present a simple effect alone as evidence of a genotype-dependent drug effect
Name the reference level of each factor beside every results table
Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the unshrunken estimate and its standard error in the table
State that the FDR is controlled within each contrast, not across the three contrasts
State the method dependence of the enrichment results and present enriched sets as hypotheses
Include the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
caveats: A difference in significance between the WT and KO simple effects is not a significant difference between them — this is the most common misreading of a 2x2 and the report must pre-empt it
No transcript-length offset was available (gene-level matrix input), which the report must disclose alongside the salmon provenance

grounding.reason: Interaction design report: simple effects and interaction contrast side by side (R-0092@bb58), fit diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085@c24d), enrichment provenance (R-0051@01ca) and reproducibility record (R-0086@becf).
